package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via installers and phishing sites, not a software package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The malware is designed to inject payloads into system processes, deploy rootkits, block security software, exfiltrate personal and financial data, and facilitate large-scale credential and credit card phishing campaigns. It employs multiple evasion and persistence techniques, and is distributed via deceptive installers and phishing websites.

execution_context.file_location: malicious installer (downloaded from software sharing website)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Encoded URLs in installer → decode → download CopperStealth dropper → execute dropper
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At installation time, the installer decodes embedded URLs, downloads additional payloads (including the CopperStealth dropper), and executes them, enabling further infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Installers should not download and execute hidden payloads from encoded URLs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal installers only install the advertised software, not hidden malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may fetch updates, but with user consent and integrity checks.
key_indicators: Silent download and execution of additional binaries

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Rootkit driver with IRP_MJ_CREATE, IRP_MJ_READ, IRP_MJ_SHUTDOWN handlers; injects payloads into explorer.exe and other processes.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At system startup or post-install, the rootkit registers as a file system filter driver, injects code into system processes, and blocks execution of certain drivers and access to registry keys.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Rootkit behavior is inherently malicious, especially when used to inject code and block security tools.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate drivers do not inject code into unrelated processes or block security software.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some security products use filter drivers, but with transparency and user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: DriverEntry: if blacklisted byte sequence found in driver, modify entry point to return STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At driver load time, the rootkit scans for blacklisted byte sequences (associated with security vendors) and sabotages their loading by forcing STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Actively sabotaging security software is a hallmark of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal drivers do not interfere with other drivers' loading.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Increase HKCU\Software\Microsoft\count_a0b1c2d3; check internet via hxxp://www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt; report to hxxp://cnzz_url&m=<machine ID>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware increments a registry counter, checks for internet connectivity, collects a unique machine ID, and exfiltrates statistics to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited data exfiltration and registry modification are suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not silently report unique IDs to third-party servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry in legitimate software, but with user consent and privacy policy.
key_indicators: Outbound connection to suspicious telemetry server

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Web browser program uses Internet Explorer object and SHDocVwCtl class to extract 'checkcode' input and send exit message via pipes if correct.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the phishing browser collects user input (confirmation code) and communicates with the main payload to control process flow based on victim interaction.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Custom browser windows collecting sensitive input and controlling malware persistence is highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate browsers do not control malware payloads or require confirmation codes for network restoration.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: HTML form requesting cardholder name, credit card number, expiration date, CVV, address, phone, etc.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At user interaction, the phishing page collects sensitive credit card and personal information and submits it to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Webpages mimicking Microsoft and requesting full credit card details are classic phishing.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Microsoft pages never request full credit card details for network restoration.

attack_chain.action: Victim downloads malicious installer from a software sharing website.
Installer decodes URLs, downloads CopperStealth dropper, and executes it.
CopperStealth rootkit installs as a file system filter driver, injects payloads, and blocks security software.
Statistics module collects machine ID, checks connectivity, and exfiltrates data.
CopperPhish phishing browser is launched, presenting fake Microsoft pages to the victim.
Victim is tricked into entering sensitive credit card and personal information.

behavioral_signatures: Installer decoding and downloading additional payloads from encoded URLs
Rootkit driver registering as a file system filter and injecting into explorer.exe
Blocking of security vendor drivers via byte sequence scanning
Silent registry modification and outbound telemetry to suspicious domains
Custom browser windows with no close/minimize, collecting sensitive input
Phishing pages impersonating Microsoft and requesting full credit card details
file_indicators: Presence of unknown drivers with IRP_MJ_CREATE/READ/SHUTDOWN handlers
network_indicators: Phishing domains such as 0zpt4.za.com, newappsofthq.site, pharmadescuento.com
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installers that decode and download additional payloads, rootkit driver registration, and process injection into explorer.exe. Detect registry modifications to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\count_a0b1c2d3 and outbound connections to known telemetry and phishing domains. Flag custom browser windows that cannot be closed and collect sensitive information, especially those impersonating Microsoft. Use network and file IOCs to block and quarantine affected systems.
